title.narrative: Supporting institutional and human capacities towards adopting media and information literacy (MIL) Against Conflict-Driving Disinformation

description.narrative: Nigeria faces a rapidly escalating risk of misinformation, disinformation, and hate speech, particularly in the lead-up to the 2027 general elections. Monitoring by the National Orientation Agency, independent fact-checking organizations, and social media analytics indicate that viral disinformation has surged by over 40% in key Northern and urban states, disproportionately affecting youth, women, and marginalized communities. Past election cycles demonstrate that misinformation contributes to local tensions, communal violence, and the disruption of democratic processes, with social cohesion and public safety particularly threatened in rural and peri-urban communities where viral narratives can escalate rapidly. It is imperative that stakeholders and citizens exhibit a range of functional and critical thinking skills related to Media and Information Literacy required to navigate the complex information landscape, fostering critical thinking, civic engagement, and ethical behavior towards achieving citizen effectiveness in the 21st century. This workplan aims at strengthening youth organizations, educational institutions, and media as frontline actors in Nigeria’s information ecosystem. By embedding critical Media and Information Literacy (MIL) competencies, these actors will be empowered to verify, interpret, and disseminate accurate information across digital and grassroots platforms, mitigating misinformation before it spreads.
